faq.q: Why does the casino always win?
faq.a: Every bet has a slightly negative expected value for the player. Over thousands of bets the average result gets very close to that, so the casino steadily collects about 2.7 percent of all money bet.

faq.q: Why does the green zero matter?
faq.a: Without it, red and black would be exactly 50-50 and the game fair. The zero makes you lose on 19 pockets but win on only 18.
asks: What is the zero for in roulette?

faq.q: What is the house edge in roulette?
faq.a: On a European wheel with one zero, it is 1 over 37, about 2.7 percent. American wheels have a double zero too, making it about 5.3 percent.
asks: How much does the casino keep?

faq.q: What is the expected value of a bet on red?
faq.a: Win 1 coin with chance 18 over 37, lose 1 with chance 19 over 37. Expected value is 18 over 37 minus 19 over 37, which is minus 1 over 37 of a coin.
No. Every spin is independent, so no pattern of bets can change the negative expected value. Doubling your bet after losses only risks huge losses.

facts: A European roulette wheel has 37 pockets: 18 red, 18 black and one green zero.
The house edge on European roulette is 1/37, about 2.7%.
